title: Cox Farms
description: Working farm with seasonal festivals, corn maze, slides, hayrides, and farm animals. Famous for the Fall Festival and Fields of Fear Halloween event.
parentHacks: The big slides are worth the wait - adults can go too!
Go on a weekday if possible - weekends are packed
Wear shoes you don't mind getting muddy
The corn maze has an easy path marked for little ones

title: Fairfax Ice Arena
description: Year-round ice skating facility offering public skating sessions, hockey leagues, and figure skating classes. Skate rentals available. Check schedule for public session times.
parentHacks: Call ahead to confirm public skate times - schedule changes often
Rental skates are included in admission
Bring thick socks - rental skates can be cold and uncomfortable
The snack bar has decent hot chocolate

title: Go Ape Zipline & Adventure Park
description: Outdoor treetop adventure course featuring ziplines, rope ladders, Tarzan swings, and obstacles. Two courses available: one for adults/teens and a junior course for ages 5+.

schedule.seasonalNotes: Weekends only in spring/fall. Closed Dec-Feb.

parentHacks: The junior course is perfect for kids 5-12 and includes supervision
Wear closed-toe shoes - no sandals allowed
Book weeks in advance for weekends
Bring layers - it's cooler up in the trees

title: Great Country Farms
description: Family farm offering seasonal pick-your-own produce, farm animals, hayrides, and a massive playground. Special events throughout the year including pumpkin patches and sunflower festivals.
parentHacks: The giant slides are worth the trek up the hill
Bring a wagon for hauling produce and tired toddlers
Arrive when they open to beat the crowds
Pack snacks - food options are limited and lines get long

title: KidScience Labs Fairfax
description: Hands-on science enrichment center offering classes, camps, and drop-in lab sessions. Kids conduct real experiments in chemistry, physics, biology, and engineering.
parentHacks: Drop-in sessions fill up fast - call ahead to reserve a spot
Kids get to take home what they make/create
Great option for birthday parties
Wear clothes that can get messy

title: Launch Trampoline Park
description: Indoor trampoline park featuring wall-to-wall trampolines, foam pits, dodgeball courts, ninja warrior courses, and a dedicated area for younger jumpers. Perfect for burning energy on rainy days.
parentHacks: Buy the special grip socks online beforehand - cheaper than at the door
Weekday mornings are much less crowded
The toddler area is separate and safe from big kids
Bring water bottles - they have fill stations

title: LEGO Discovery Center
description: Interactive LEGO attraction featuring rides, 4D cinema, building workshops, and millions of LEGO bricks. Designed for families with children ages 3-10.
parentHacks: Book online in advance for the best price - walk-up is expensive
Adults must be accompanied by a child (no solo adult visits)
The 4D cinema is loud - might scare sensitive little ones
2-3 hours is plenty of time for most families

title: Mosaic District Playground & Splash Pad
description: Modern outdoor playground and seasonal splash pad in the heart of Mosaic District. Surrounded by restaurants and shops. Free to enjoy.
parentHacks: Parking garage validates first 2 hours free with purchase
Ted's Bulletin across the street has great brunch
Bring a change of clothes for splash pad days
The playground has good shade coverage

title: National Museum of Natural History
description: World-renowned museum featuring dinosaur fossils, the Hope Diamond, live butterfly pavilion, and hands-on discovery rooms. Free admission makes it perfect for repeat visits.
parentHacks: The Butterfly Pavilion has timed tickets - get them first thing
Q?rius on the ground floor is perfect for hands-on exploration
Take the Metro - parking nearby is expensive and limited
Download the museum app for kid-friendly scavenger hunts

title: Reston Zoo
description: Small family-friendly zoo with farm animals, exotic species, pony rides, and a petting area. Educational programs and birthday party options available.
parentHacks: Pony rides are extra but the kids love them
Small enough to see everything in 1.5-2 hours
The picnic area is nice for packed lunches
Not much shade - bring hats and sunscreen in summer

title: Roer's Zoofari
description: Family-owned zoo featuring exotic animals from around the world. Get up close with giraffes, zebras, and lemurs. Feed animals and enjoy the petting zoo area.
parentHacks: Buy animal feed at the entrance - kids love feeding the animals
The giraffe feeding is a must-do experience
Weekday mornings are much quieter
Mostly flat paths - stroller friendly

title: Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center
description: Explore the companion facility to the National Air and Space Museum featuring thousands of aviation and space artifacts including the Space Shuttle Discovery, a Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird, and the Boeing B-29 Superfortress Enola Gay.
parentHacks: Free parking lot fills up by 11am on weekends - arrive early
The flight simulators are extra cost but worth it for older kids
Pack a lunch - the cafe is pricey and limited

title: Zava Zone
description: Multi-level indoor playground designed for kids 12 and under. Features climbing structures, slides, ball pits, and a separate toddler area. Great for birthday parties and play dates.
parentHacks: Adults don't pay if they're not playing - just supervising
Socks required - they sell them if you forget
The toddler section is perfect for little ones away from big kids
Check for Groupon deals before you go

Reading sessions cannot be extended due to late arrival. This program is for ages 6-12. Registration is required."

title: Family Storytime
description: Tysons-Pimmit Meeting Room 1, Tysons-Pimmit Meeting Room 2 Tysons-Pimmit Regional Library Experience the joy of playful learning. Children and their caregivers participate in music, movement and song in this program that highlights the natural rhythms in language. Space limited to 25 children with up to two caregivers per child. No registration. Entrance tickets are provided first come, first served at the Information Desk 30 minutes before the program begins. For children from birth to 5 years.

title: Saturday Stories
description: Richard Byrd Library Join us in the children's area for a storytime designed for families with children ages birth to five. No registration required.

title: Saturday Morning Storytime

Read, sing, learn, dance and have fun at the library with our friends at Tiny Dancers in Fairfax City studio. This program is designed for kids ages 3 to 5. Ticket required for entry. title: Kids Writing Club
description: Registration required. resenter: volunteer Great Falls Conference Room Great Falls Library Are you an aspiring author? Learn how to get a creative writing project started in an encouraging environment. Ages 8 - 12 years old. Registration encouraged, not required.

title: STEAM Makerspace - Chemistry for Ages 5-7
description: Registration required. Meeting Room (E103) Kingstowne Regional Library Join us for a fun-filled Makerspace activity where science meets creativity! Explore the exciting world of chemistry through hands-on experiments, colorful reactions, and fascinating discoveries. Get ready to mix, fizz, and experiment while learning the science behind the magic. All materials will be provided! Ages:5 to 7 Registration is required. Please make sure to arrive on time.

title: STEAM Makerspace - Light up and Launch!
description: Registration required. Kingstowne Regional Library Join us for a fun- filled Makerspace activity featuring creativity, crafting and engineering! Participants will create colorful yarn basket, decorate them with battery- operated tea lights, and build mini catapults to launch their creations towards a target. Come explore the fun of combining art and science in this exciting activity. All materials will be provided. Ages: 8-11 Please arrive on time as the program is scheduled only for an hour.

title: STEAM Team - Meet the League of SI Superheroes!
description: resenter: Tamara Neifeld Burke Centre Meeting Room 116, Burke Centre Meeting Room 117 Burke Centre Library Superheroes with the powers of measurement fight against uncertainty in a creative world built by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). title: STEAM--Build Your Own Plane
description: Registration required. Lorton Meeting Room Lorton Library Grades K-6 Develop skills of Force and Motion through building a plane. We provide the materials, and you make your very own plane to fly and take home. Registration Registration required.

title: D&D Club: Saturday Morning Campaigns
description: Registration required. resenter: Kendall Hall Kings Park Meeting Room Kings Park Library Ragnarok is coming! Odin has sent you and your crew to the mystical island of Cassius to plunder, pillage, and find worthy souls to join his army in the coming apocalypse! Play as viking raiders in an open-world sandbox that reacts to the party's choices. title: Pop-Up Storytime
description: Reston Children's Department Reston Regional Library Come enjoy a Saturday morning at the library! Join Reston Youth Services staff for stories and songs! All ages welcome; children must be accompanied by an adult.

title: Spanish Bilingual Storytime
description: Pohick Meeting Room 1, Pohick Meeting Room 2 Pohick Regional Library Bienvenidos! Join us for storytime in both English and Spanish. We will read books, sing songs, and do activities to build your child's early literacy skills. Children ages 0-6 with adult are welcome.

title: Artist Playground
description: Herndon Fortnightly Maker Lab Herndon Fortnightly Library Do you enjoy crafting? Do you want to explore new ideas and play with materials? Join us at the Artist Playground for a themed craft and coloring page. Kids 6-12 with an adult.

title: Read to the Dog with PAL
description: Registration required. resenter: Marta Steenstra Davis Dolley Madison Meeting Room 1, Dolley Madison Meeting Room 2 Dolley Madison Library Join us as we welcome Daisy and Raven, two very special therapy dogs, to Dolley Madison! Dogs are certified and trained through PAL (People. Animals. Love.). This program will repeat on the second

title: LEGO Club
description: Thomas Jefferson Meeting Room 1, Thomas Jefferson Meeting Room 2 Thomas Jefferson Library Do you love LEGO? Use our huge selection of LEGO pieces to build to your heart's content! Draw a Challenge Card for inspiration, dig into our collection of LEGO books, or build freely from your own imagination. Best of all, meet new friends and socialize with kids who love LEGO just as much as you do. Ages 6-12.

title: India Across Borders Cultural Awareness Event
description: Registration required. resenter: Kaashvi Kasera 10th grade Oakton Meeting Room 1, Oakton Meeting Room 2 Oakton Library Come to Oakton library and learn about the Indian heritage and culture by celebrating Diwali, the Festival of Lights! There will be Bollywood dance lessons, henna tattoos, rangoli art, Diya decorating, and snacks. All are welcome! Led by a teen group promoting ethic cultural awareness to foster cultural understanding and inclusivity.

description: Registration required. Martha Washington Meeting Room Martha Washington Library You can create your own comic characters with simple shapes! That’s up to you! Following the event there will be a 15 minute conversation and a book signing with the author. Books will be available for sale from Scrawl Book

description: Thomas Jefferson Library Read aloud to Lucy, a trained therapy dog. Bring your own book or choose a book from the library. Walk-ins welcome.
